title: Batching and Scheduling
summary: Decode is memory-bound, so serving many users in the same step is almost free until it is not. This lesson builds the batch-size trade-off from first principles, then covers continuous batching, PagedAttention, Little's law for concurrency, and the scheduling policies that keep latency predictable.
objectives: Model decode step time as a function of batch size and compute server throughput and per-user speed
Explain why static batching wastes GPU time and how continuous (iteration-level) batching fixes it
Quantify KV-cache fragmentation and explain how PagedAttention removes it
Use Little's law to relate request rate, latency and concurrent sequences
Choose a batch limit and scheduling policy (chunked prefill, preemption, priorities) for a latency SLO
prerequisites: This lesson uses the decode step-time formula and KV bytes per token from [Where the Time Goes](/learn/inference-and-serving/memory-and-compute), and TTFT, TPOT and goodput from [Measuring Inference](/learn/inference-and-serving/measuring-inference).
